decisions.reason: recycle() retains renderer listeners and this.props after logical unmount. Async map-library initialization also has an unguarded rejection callback. Wrapper layout updates already handle ordinary prop replacement, but do not retire those paths.

Both wrappers mutate thisRef.current.props during render. SDK callbacks can read a suspended render before commit. Normal removal does not address that gap; the facade error callback shares the same converted-event path.
Both wrappers mutate thisRef.current.props during render while open. They already detach close before removal; the retained guard is for committed-callback isolation, not duplicated normal teardown.
Both wrappers mutate their props ref during render. The guard prevents an SDK result from reaching uncommitted application callbacks.

decisions.decision: keep one record; remove outer flushFeatureState guard
decisions.reason: RNMapbox class event methods read mutable this.props. A suspended class update can expose uncommitted callbacks. report.onError already protects asynchronous feature-state reset errors, so guarding the synchronous frame entry duplicates it.
Facade reportRegion may deliver onMove and onMoveEnd from one native event. An earlier application callback may synchronously detach the map before the next delivery.

The functional wrapper forwards current handlers to Fabric native host props, with no JavaScript callback registry or deferred event dispatch. Facade click-query lifetimes remain guarded in useMapInteractions.

decisions.callbacks: flushFeatureState and its asynchronous error callback
decisions.decision: remove guarded synchronous entry; retain one guarded error reporter
decisions.reason: The native frame handler starts facade-owned asynchronous resets. Only their eventual error report needs the guard.

decisions.callbacks: GeoJSON and vector press, four sites
decisions.reason: Native event delivery is wrapper-owned. These closures only normalize and dispatch a stable source id through a stable map-session dispatcher. Application source callbacks are stored by the shared Source during layout commit; asynchronous hit-query ownership remains in useMapInteractions, including replacement and unmount checks.

decisions.decision: remove guard record; keep useMemo for renderer isolation
decisions.reason: Adapters already own their required event guards. This provider synchronously observes those notifications and owns no delayed event source.

decisions.decision: remove shared guard; keep guard only on RNMapbox annotation selection
decisions.reason: Live touches and MapLibre annotations use current native host handlers. RNMapbox PointAnnotation instead reads class this.props; the annotation-local guard also covers the composed marker selection handler.

Facade-owned long-press timers and project/unproject promises can complete after callback props change. Generation/sequence checks retire stale gesture work; the record supplies current committed handlers and teardown protection.
The facade map subscription retains requestClose across callback updates; the same function is also a native button handler, so useEffectEvent is not a replacement for this shared entry.
Open is invoked only by the mounting layout effect; React supplies current committed callback access without a separate mounted guard.
Facade getZoom, zoomTo and easeTo promises can reject after the control unmounts.
The effect active flag retires superseded work, but its passive cleanup may run after layout unmount and promise settlement. The layout-owned callback guard suppresses errors in that gap.
The projection effect retires superseded work with its active flag. The parent NativeMarker error reporter retains its layout-owned callback guard for unmount protection.
Camera acknowledgments may reject after unmount; a scheduled frame needs the latest committed target; an application onMove may detach the map before the adapter calls its movement observer.

schedule is entered through current native callbacks or guarded movement and its frame is canceled on cleanup. onCommand only updates a ref; native adapter cleanup clears the command observer. Neither needs a separate latest-props or mounted guard.

The current ref stores committed props. Request active and generation checks reject detached/provider-replaced work; retirement also rechecks active after abort and release, which can synchronously unmount the control.

otherLifetimeChecks.reason: Facade-owned query promises, independent subscriptions and application-provided location services require logical attachment, generation and disposal checks.
Facade acquisition deadlines, app-state listener ownership, asynchronous observer attachment and per-subscriber disposal are not supplied by wrapper singleton services.
Pending captures, serialized feature-state operations and image loads outlive their initiating call and need explicit facade resource ownership.
